requirement: Run destructive-delete/tombstone/permanent-purge courts with explicit recoverability truth.
invariants: Normal workspace delete is D2 recoverable destructive and names an exact current canonical checkpoint recovery point.
Recoverable delete fences late local VFS mutations and rejects a recovery point that became stale after a newer cross-context publication.
Tombstoned workspace boot and canonical checkpoint publication are blocked until explicit restoration.
Lifecycle metadata is SHA-256 integrity-bound; corrupted lifecycle truth fails closed instead of silently reopening deleted state.
Permanent purge is a separate D4 action requiring target-specific confirmation that recoverability becomes none.
Permanent purge physically removes workspace storage and leaves only non-content lifecycle mutation truth with recoverable=false.
Duplicate delete/purge mutation identities are idempotent; different mutation identities cannot silently replace prior destructive intent.
Purge acknowledgement loss exposes an unknown outcome and authoritative reconciliation determines the terminal purged state before retry.
